set.body:
## Outcome and ownership
Audit, qualify and where necessary improve ScalaFIM's existing general-purpose volume-to-surface machinery for exact group-volume reference spaces and standard cortical families, initially fsLR 32k. Owner: ScalaFIM surface/spatial/view maintainers. P1; implementation and new qualification not yet started. PLSNeuro selects available qualified routes, supplies result context and presents/export receipts; it must not own a duplicate mapping kernel or transform engine.

## Existing functionality to reuse
Inspect current candidates and the exact consumer pin, not only the older primary checkout. PLSNeuro at 96cb12a uses ScalaFIM 7c3ff0a0edc92be0e2fe35c431d5b9e458c92ab4. Existing modules/surface SurfaceSampling.scala provides VolumeSurfaceSamplingPlan, VolumeSurfaceSampler, white/pial/midpoint/fractional-thickness/normal-line sampling, reducers, masks and inspectVertex/inspectVertexEither receipts. VolToSurfMorphism and modules/surface-view SurfaceVolumeProjection materialize values/quality/work receipts on corresponding display geometry. Consumer SurfaceProjection.project/inspect already delegates to these APIs.
Existing tests: SurfaceSamplingSuite, SurfaceSamplingReceiptSuite and SurfaceProjectionNetworkSuite. Closed native footprint issue bd-01M1STGTHBJP6ZD7HGTMEGP9NE records earlier evidence; do not recreate its completed scope. In the inspected pinned implementation, each point uses nearest-voxel lookup; averaging sampled depths is not proof of voxel-overlap ribbon-constrained projection. Audit actual capabilities and numerical contracts before choosing defaults or adding algorithms.

## Scope and acceptance
1. Inventory the existing public sampling, spatial pullback/transform and projection APIs and their exact tests. Distinguish point interpolation from aggregation along depth, label versus continuous data, missing/nonfinite semantics, duplicate voxel contributions, coordinate transforms and any ribbon support. Record gaps without assuming a new kernel is needed.
2. Admit source volume reference explicitly: exact template variant/version, voxel-to-world affine/grid/units and analysis support. Identify the sampling geometry's own coordinate reference, hemisphere, ordered topology, medial-wall mask and transforms. An MNI string or fsLR density is not correspondence evidence. Reject ambiguous references, reversed/incompatible transform chains, wrong hemispheres or mismatched masks/topology.
3. Qualify an exact route for the actual group analysis space into fsLR 32k. Preserve original group-volume statistics. Derived cortical display is not surface-native inference. Resolve whether existing point sampling is adequate for the declared use; compare justified interpolation/projection alternatives against an independent implementation where needed. True ribbon methods require corresponding inner/outer anatomy and a defined weighting rule; midthickness alone must not be relabelled ribbon mapping.
4. Keep anatomical sampling/mapping separate from inflated/veryinflated display coordinates. The same mapped values, coverage and vertex IDs must survive display switches. Atlas supplies labels/provenance, TemplateFlow4s acquires exact assets, ScalaFIM executes/adopts general geometry and mapping machinery; neither atlas nor the app duplicates acquisition/projection.
5. Independent numeric tests: asymmetric coordinate ramps/impulses and known transforms; oblique, anisotropic and shifted grids; exact reference mismatch; edges/outside support; medial wall; finite/nonfinite/masked/zero values; continuous versus categorical policies. Preserve/expose per-vertex contribution evidence sufficient to reconstruct results and link picks back to contributing volume locations. Do not infer validity from screenshots.
6. Freeze numerical and coverage budgets before evaluating real data. Then run real group beta/FIR fixtures in their precisely identified space, matched anatomy/coverage review, stable value identity across inflated/veryinflated, correct pick footprints and source-bound exports. JVM and Scala.js/required optimized-JS tests, applicable native gates, bounded memory/timing and exact provider closure are required for admission. Existing test source is not a new pass; this planning ticket runs no tests.
7. Expose enough typed capability/provenance for consumers to rank only qualified routes for a given source reference and available assets, disclose chosen route and refuse unavailable mappings. Qualify each additional template/space route separately; do not silently resample through a generic MNI alias.

## Consumer sequence and prerequisites
Foreign consumer owner: /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro/.mote bd-01M2421N7AZQX1AK5BEMVSB84K (P1 standard family). First compare fsLR 32k inflated and veryinflated with raw normals, matched three-light conditions, medial-wall masking and synthetic overlays; introduce real beta/FIR only after their mapping route qualifies. Exact assets/coordinate metadata and any needed anatomical pair or transform are prerequisites to that specific route, not reasons to duplicate or guess coordinates.
Smoothing is a separate optional capability: defer tuning the single-subject regression mesh and any smoothing-default decision until the standard-family comparison. This ticket does not depend on smoothing. General smoothing remains mesh4s-owned; native ScalaFIM smoothing integration bd-01M34K30H3PZ1PDZRHZH7HK7YG is separate. Existing mesh4s migration candidates must be reconciled explicitly if they are relevant; no unreviewed provider switch.
No cross-store blocking edges, changes to inference, publication, or full V4 closure are implied.
set.title: Audit and qualify existing volume-to-surface mapping for exact group spaces and fsLR
